concept.name: Price impact in AMMs
concept.definition: Price impact is the change in a pool's token price caused by a trader's own swap: under the constant-product rule, larger trades relative to pool depth execute at progressively worse prices, and the impact is deterministic given pool reserves.
concept.intuition: It is how much your own order moves the market against you — the bigger the bite you take from the pool, the worse the price of the last bite.
concept.mechanics: In a CPMM, output is Δy = y·Δx/(x+Δx), so average execution price worsens as Δx grows relative to reserve x; price impact ≈ Δx/(x+Δx) for small trades, growing quadratically. Unlike slippage (which includes other trades landing first), price impact is caused solely by your own trade and is shown by DEX interfaces before signing.
concept.formula: For x·y=k, output Δy = y·Δx / (x + Δx); impact ≈ 1 − (execution price / spot price) = Δx / (x + Δx).
concept.failure_modes: In thin pools even modest trades move prices several percent, and a single large swap can be exploited as a temporary oracle price for attacks on dependent protocols; splitting orders reduces but cannot eliminate impact.
concept.misconceptions: Price impact is not a fee — it is an execution cost paid through a worse exchange rate, and it is not the same as slippage, which also includes price movement from other actors before your trade confirms.
concept.example: A pool holds 10 ETH and 40,000 USDC (spot 4,000). A 10,000 USDC buy (25% of USDC depth) returns 2 ETH at an average 5,000 USDC/ETH — a 25% price impact, versus ~0% impact for a tiny trade.

citations.source: Uniswap Support - Price Impact vs. Price Slippage
